note: Hand-written. Example words are vocab.json entries (strongs + lemma, checked by scripts/build-greek-course.js); an optional form is an inflected spelling that occurs in orig/nt under that lemma. exampleRefs are verse references whose text comes from orig/ at display time. Sound-alikes are American English.

transliteration.scheme: STEPBible TAGNT (the t field of orig/nt), reproduced by translit() in scripts/build-greek-course.js
transliteration.summary: One Latin letter or pair per Greek letter: η = ē and ω = ō (macron marks the long vowel), θ th, φ ph, χ ch, ψ ps, ξ x, υ u (never y), ζ z. γγ = ng; γκ, γξ, γχ keep the g (gk, gx, gch). Rough breathing = h, written before the whole diphthong (houtos); initial ρ = rh. Smooth breathing, accents and iota subscript are not written. After an initial h-vowel that does not join the next vowel, an apostrophe marks the break (he'autou, he'ōrakamen).
transliteration.dataQuirk: The TAGNT text drops the h when a rough breathing and an accent sit on the same iota or diphthong (ina for ἵνα, aimatos for αἵματος, oitines for οἵτινες). vocab.json applies the scheme as stated (hina) and records the text's own spelling as translitInText.

letters.name: gamma
letters.sound: hard g; before γ, κ, ξ or χ it is n as in sing
letters.soundAlike: γ = g as in got (γγ = ng as in finger)

letters.name: eta
letters.sound: long e, like the a in late

letters.name: iota
letters.soundAlike: ι = i as in intrigue (short) or machine (long)

letters.name: rho
letters.sound: r, lightly rolled; at the start of a word it always has a rough breathing (rh)
letters.soundAlike: ρ = a single flick of the tongue, like the tt in American 'butter'

letters.name: sigma
letters.sound: s (never z); written ς at the end of a word
letters.soundAlike: σ, ς = s as in study

letters.name: upsilon
letters.sound: ü as in German über: say ee with rounded lips (many teachers simply say oo)
letters.soundAlike: υ = ü as in French tu

letters.name: chi
letters.sound: throaty ch (a k sound is acceptable)
letters.soundAlike: χ = ch as in Scottish loch

letters.name: psi
letters.sound: ps, also at the start of a word
letters.noExampleNote: None of the 150 vocabulary words has a ψ; 1 John 1:1 and 1:6 each have one (we have touched; we lie).

diphthongs.noExampleNote: Rare; none of the 150 vocabulary words has it.

iotaSubscript.description: A small iota written under a long vowel. It is not pronounced and not transliterated: read ᾳ as α, ῃ as η, ῳ as ω. It often marks the dative case.

breathings.name: smooth breathing
breathings.description: On every word that starts with a vowel or diphthong and has no h sound. Not pronounced, not transliterated.

breathings.name: rough breathing
breathings.description: Adds an h before the vowel. A word starting with υ always has it, and so does a word starting with ρ (transliterated rh).

breathings.name: breathing on a diphthong
breathings.description: The breathing sits on the second vowel of a diphthong but belongs to the whole syllable.

breathings.name: breathing on a capital
breathings.description: On a capital letter the breathing (and accent) is written before it, at the top left.

accents.description: Three accent marks show the stressed syllable (in Erasmian reading, stress the accented syllable). You do not need to write them. They seldom change the meaning, but a few pairs differ only by accent.

marks.name: grave
marks.description: An acute on the last syllable turns grave when another word follows without punctuation.

marks.name: circumflex
marks.description: Only on long vowels and diphthongs.

accentPair.description: τίς (accented) asks who? or what?; τις (no accent of its own) means someone or a certain.

enclitics.description: Some short words lean on the word before and often lose their accent, so ἐστίν is usually printed ἐστιν.

otherMarks.name: diaeresis
otherMarks.description: Two dots over ι or υ: the vowel is said on its own, not as part of a diphthong.
otherMarks.noExampleNote: None of the 150 vocabulary words has one; John 1:23 has the name Isaiah.

otherMarks.name: elision
otherMarks.description: A short final vowel is dropped before a word that starts with a vowel and an apostrophe takes its place; before a rough breathing the consonant may also change (μετά → μεθ᾽).

otherMarks.name: movable nu
otherMarks.description: Some endings (‑σι, and ‑ε in the 3rd singular) can add a ν. It does not change the meaning. The NA27 text used here nearly always prints it, so expect ἐστιν and εἰσιν; paradigm tables show it as (ν).

punctuation.name: full stop
punctuation.meaning: end of a sentence, as in English

punctuation.name: Greek question mark
punctuation.meaning: a question mark — it looks like an English semicolon

punctuationNote: The STEP text in orig/ keeps the raised dot and the question mark but no commas or full stops, so only those two appear when verse text is shown.
